name: Tiglath-Pileser
bio:
Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria, also called Pul, first invaded Israel in Menahem's reign; Menahem bought his support with a thousand talents of silver raised from Israel's wealthy, and Tiglath-Pileser withdrew without staying in the land (2 Kings 15:19-20). Later, in Pekah's reign, Tiglath-Pileser returned and captured Ijon, Abel Beth Maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee, and all the land of Naphtali, carrying the people into exile in Assyria (2 Kings 15:29).

## 📖 Core Story: Rescuing Ahaz, Destroying Damascus

When Ahaz, king of Judah, appealed to Tiglath-Pileser for rescue from Syria and Israel, calling himself Assyria's servant and son and sending temple and palace treasure as tribute, Tiglath-Pileser obliged: he attacked Damascus, captured it, deported its people to Kir, and killed Rezin, king of Syria. Ahaz then traveled to Damascus to meet him, where he saw a pagan altar whose design he later had copied in the Jerusalem temple (2 Kings 16:7-10).
